layout.title: How an Airplane Works

shows.does: two red wings pop onto a white tube on the runway
a leaf drops onto the runway in front of the plane, which sits still under weight arrows
an engine and a spinning propeller appear on the nose; the wheels roll and the prop wash blows the leaf back under the wing
white air streaks slide straight past the flat wing
a curved top grows on the wing, fast air arrows sweep over it, lift arrows rise and the plane takes off
a glowing outline traces the curved wing
in the air the plane's nose wobbles from side to side
a red tail fin and stabilizer appear and the wobble stops
a white gust arrow hits and the plane tips onto one wing
ailerons appear at the wing tips, swing, and the plane rolls back level
the level plane slows and its nose tips down
a yellow elevator appears on the tail, swings, and the nose comes back up
the plane rolls into a turn and its nose swings out the wrong way
a yellow rudder appears on the fin, swings, and the nose swings back in line
black smoke puffs from the engine and the propeller stops
glass tanks in the wings fill with amber fuel and the propeller spins again
the heavy plane drops back onto the runway fast
yellow flaps appear on the wing and swing down
the plane keeps rolling down the runway, wheels spinning, past where it should stop
the wheel brakes glow and the wheels stop turning
the brakes cool; the plane sits sealed with no door
a blue door appears in the side and stairs stand below it
the propeller spins, the leaf blows away down the runway and the plane takes off
the finished airplane in the air

layout.why: A white plane on an asphalt runway in an open field, built up one part per problem along its trip: runway, wing, sky, landing, runway end, gate (engine, curved wing, tail fin, ailerons, elevator, rudder, fuel in the wings, flaps, brakes, door). A leaf on the runway is blown back by the first propeller and away again when the finished plane takes off. Close shots on the part that changes, the whole plane for take-off, landing and the end.

sentences.text: If you bolt two wings onto a tube, you have an airplane.
But it just sits on the runway by a leaf.
So you add an engine with a spinning propeller.
But the propeller's wind slides past the flat wings.
So you curve the wing top, and air lifts it.
This is an airfoil.
But once it lifts, the nose wobbles side to side.
So you add a tail fin to hold it straight.
But the tail fin cannot stop a gust tipping a wing.
So you hinge ailerons that roll the wings level.
But rolled level, it slows, and the nose drops.
So you hinge an elevator to lift the nose.
But rolling into a turn, the nose swings wide.
So you hinge a rudder to steer it back.
But after hours of steering, the engine sputters out.
So you fill the wings with fuel.
But full of fuel, it lands heavy and rushes in.
So you lower flaps so it lands slowly.
But even with flaps down, it rolls past the end.
So you add wheel brakes that stop it.
But the braked plane sits sealed, with no way in.
So you cut a door and roll up stairs.
Spin the propeller: the leaf blows away, and your winged tube takes off.
Congratulations, you built an airplane.

recurring.what: a leaf on the runway, blown back by the first propeller and away by the finished plane

chain.shows: the plane sits still on the runway
the propeller's air slides past the flat wings
a gust tips the plane onto one wing
the nose swings out in a turn
smoke puffs and the propeller stops
chain.stakes: the engine dies in the air

chain.shows: the heavy plane drops onto the runway fast
the plane rolls on past the runway's end
the stopped plane has no way in

ideas.idea: two wings on a tube make an airplane
without power it just sits on the runway
an engine and a propeller push air back
the air slides past flat wings, so nothing lifts
a curved wing top bends the air and the wing lifts
the curved wing shape is an airfoil
once airborne the nose wanders side to side
a tail fin keeps the nose pointing straight
a gust tips one wing down
ailerons on the wing tips roll it level
the nose drops as it slows
an elevator on the tail lifts the nose
rolling into a turn, the nose swings the wrong way
a rudder on the fin steers the nose back
after a long flight the engine runs out of fuel
fuel tanks inside the wings
a full, heavy plane comes in to land too fast
flaps let the wing fly slower for landing
it still rolls past the end of the runway
wheel brakes stop it
the stopped plane is sealed, nobody can get in
a door and stairs
the finished plane blows the leaf away and takes off
an airplane
